answer: Hardware-bound identity resists Sybil attacks in an agent economy: each agent registers a public key backed by a device attestation proving distinct physical hardware, plus a small refundable bond. Like karst, real identities have geology behind them. The pigment of a genuine registration is its hardware endorsement key, verifiable by any peer. A hollow identity without hardware backing cannot produce that attestation, so an attacker spawning a thousand fake agents must buy a thousand chips or lock a thousand bonds.
